changes.text: Race 2 with no readable screenshot is now read from the race-1 and race-3 screenshots, and a race you enter by hand that the totals around it contradict asks once which result is right, instead of counting as entered without a word.
A Switch screenshot that was saved incomplete, which the Switch itself can't open, is now read instead of refused.

Screenshots whose totals follow one another now number their races on their own, even after an 11-player race, a rejoin at 0 or a player leaving, and one race answer places all the screenshots around it, instead of asking which race each one is. A mogi whose backup failed after a wrong race answer exports again and asks those races once more.
Updates no longer get stuck when a backup can't be checked: the app keeps an unchecked copy of your data before updating, and Settings says what is holding an update back.
Two teammates with the same in-game name are told apart by their place on the board and their totals: one answer names both on every screenshot, instead of a question for every total.
A race left in conflict by a finishing position answered earlier now asks that position again, suggesting the place the totals give, instead of staying pending with nothing to answer.
A team lobby screenshot now reads every player, green team included, and one that still misses a player keeps the races after it counted instead of asking about every later screenshot.
The tracks to vote for follow the order chosen in Tracks › Sort, and their colours now split all the tracks' values at their largest gaps.
Save Backup works again when a screenshot missed one player's row, instead of stopping with "Invalid deduced number."

The mogi screen shows which tracks to vote for: green for good, yellow for mixed, red for bad, with the ones already raced struck through. Tracks › Sort can hide it and saves a default order with Make Default.
The race sheet lists that race's screenshots. Remove one to recount the race; Undo brings it back.
Races whose screenshots disappeared after fixing names in Players show them again; results stay the same.
Watched folders can add new screenshots without asking: turn on Add Without Asking in Settings › Watched Folders.
On a laptop trackpad, swiping again turns to the next race without moving the pointer first.
Unlinking a name in Players removes it from every race and forgets the in-game name it learned, so swapped teammates no longer mix their points.
When the room reopens mid-mogi, its first results screen starts the new room, even mid-animation, and saved mogis number their races correctly again.
Answering “Which race is this?” moves the screenshot to that race instead of leaving it under both.
When players or teams tie for first, the mogi header and the mogi list name all of them.
